endorsements.quote: Like any technology, AI must be evaluated for its medical, social, economic, and ethical implications ( 2 ).
The doctor-patient relationship will evolve into a hybrid model where AI enhances decision-making, but human oversight remains crucial for trust and empathy ( 19 ).

Digital literacy and accessible technologies will be essential in reducing inequalities and empowering individuals to actively participate in their healthcare while maintaining the foundational humanistic values of medicine ( 20 ).

unlisted_practices: Evolve regulatory frameworks to ensure AI transparency, accountability, and equitable access.
Keep leadership of multidisciplinary AI-enabled care teams with physicians.
Prioritize patients most in need so AI-driven healthcare does not exacerbate disparities.
Adopt a multidisciplinary approach involving health professionals, policymakers, and technology developers for AI implementation.
Governments and regulators should enforce encryption, anonymization, and data access rights for health data used by AI.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/brief report discussing the future ethical challenges, regulatory needs, and deployment practices (including a fictional 2040 case study) of AI in preventive medicine.
